subject.title: Windows: Telegram voice-note STT + exec-approvals writer fail silently with EPERM on fsync/rename (no retry, no user feedback)

question: Does a supported current Windows build still reproduce Telegram inbound voice-note materialization failing with EPERM after the v2026.5.4 attachment-flush fix?
rationale: The observed logs come from 2026.5.2 and the shipped fix addresses the same filesystem failure class, but its stated coverage does not prove the Telegram inbound path is covered.

options.title: Request current-version Telegram proof
options.body: Reproduce one inbound voice note on current Windows with redacted gateway logs and identify the source attachment-write path before changing retries or channel UX.

options.title: Treat the report as covered
options.body: Close as covered by the v2026.5.4 Windows attachment fix if maintainers confirm Telegram uses that same persisted-attachment path.

recommendation.title: Request current-version Telegram proof
recommendation.body: Reproduce one inbound voice note on current Windows with redacted gateway logs and identify the source attachment-write path before changing retries or channel UX.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest adjacent history signal for the shipped Windows media persistence correction.
